references.text: Earlier in the chapter, vows and abstentions made by a woman while living in her father's house are mentioned, forming the basis for rules concerning the vows of a married woman.
The following verse explains what happens when the husband hears about her vow—he can either confirm or annul it.
The book of Moses repeats the importance of keeping vows made to the Lord and that whatever goes out of the lips must be kept.
The Preacher warns to be careful with vows to God, stating that it is better not to make a vow than to make one and fail to keep it.
God's word to the woman after the fall, saying that her desire shall be for her husband and he shall rule over her, forms the background for the man's authority over the woman's vows.
Paul mentions that a woman is bound to her husband as long as he lives, which reflects the principle of the binding nature of marriage.
